class: Pride of America class (Project America class) — Norwegian Cruise Line

zones.what: Lifeboats/tenders are slung on Deck 7 midship — the OK/OX 'Obstructed Oceanview' category exists on Deck 7 midship, and a cruise blogger who sailed the ship confirmed the boats 'jut out from the side of the ship on deck 7 and are visible below most balcony cabins and especially those located directly above them on deck 8.'
zones.effect: On Deck 7 itself the boats sit right at window/balcony level, blocking part of the view outward; on Deck 8, directly above, the horizon is clear but looking straight down at the water is blocked by the boat tops, and the boats show up in balcony photos.
zones.mattersTo: Photographers and anyone who wants an unobstructed straight-down view will notice it on Deck 8 (and more so on Deck 7); horizon-gazers and most vacationers barely notice. The blogger recommended a higher deck or a far-forward/far-aft cabin to avoid it entirely.
zones.source: profcruise.com (first-person cabin-selection blog) + seascanner.com deck-plan legend (OK category = 'deck 7, midships, obstructed view') + cruisemapper.com ('Categories OK and OX have obstructed views due to lifeboats')

zones.what: Deck 7 sits directly above the Deck 6 Mardi Gras Cabaret Lounge & Nightclub (a no-cabin entertainment deck); cabins 7522 and 7526 were specifically flagged by cruisers as sitting directly over it.
zones.effect: Reports are mixed: one Cruise Critic reviewer near the Mardi Gras room said they 'never heard a sound' because they were at the front of the ship away from the club, while a Gangwaze cabin reviewer for 7526 said it was 'directly above the Mardi Gras night club' and would 'choose deck 8 or above' next time.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and late-to-bed cruisers booking Deck 7 balcony/oceanview cabins mid-to-aft should ask about proximity to the nightclub footprint; guests who stay out late or don't mind bass won't care.
zones.source: boards.cruisecritic.co.uk thread on cabin 7522 + gangwaze.com cabin 9656 page (quoting a reviewer on cabin 7526) + cruisecritic.com member review ('never heard a sound' near Mardi Gras)

zones.what: Deck 10 sits directly beneath the Deck 11 Aloha Café buffet, South Beach Pool, and specialty dining (Little Italy/Moderno Churrascaria); a cabin 10640 reviewer wrote they 'were right below the buffet restaurant, late at night and early morning we could hear lots of noise from above us.'
zones.effect: Chair-dragging, foot traffic, and early-morning buffet setup carry down one deck; noise is concentrated at breakfast set-up hours and late-night pool/bar activity, not constant.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who value sleeping in should avoid Deck 10 mid/aft under the buffet and pool footprint; a Deck 10 aft cabin (10678) directly under the Moderno café reported no noise issue, so it varies by exact spot.
zones.source: cruiseline.com cabin 10640 review ('right below the buffet restaurant... lots of noise from above') + cruisecritic.com review of cabin 10678 (no noise issue under Moderno café) + cruisemapper/NCL venue placement (Aloha Café & South Beach Pool on Deck 11)

zones.what: The ship's main circulation hub is the Capitol Atrium, described by CruiseMapper as an 'eight-deck midship hub' housing the central elevator bank (10 elevators total across the ship).
zones.effect: Cabins near the midship atrium/elevator bank get the shortest walk to dining, theater, and the Capitol Atrium, at the cost of some hallway and lobby noise/traffic.
zones.mattersTo: Guests with mobility needs or who want convenience benefit from booking near this bank; light sleepers wanting quiet should ask for a cabin a few doors away rather than immediately adjacent. One Cruise Critic reviewer specifically praised cabin 7668 as 'a great position - no noise and close to lifts.'
zones.source: cruisemapper.com ('eight-deck midship hub', '10 elevators') + cruisecritic.com member review of cabin 7668

zones.what: Propulsion is two Rolls-Royce Mermaid electric propulsion pods mounted aft under the hull, per the ship's technical specifications.
zones.effect: Pod (as opposed to traditional shaft) propulsion generally transmits less vibration into aft cabins than older shaft-driven ships, but Deck 4 — the lowest guest deck and closest to the machinery spaces — is the most exposed to any residual hum or vibration at speed.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests should be aware Deck 4 aft is the closest guest deck to the propulsion pods, though pod drives make this less of an issue than on older tonnage.
zones.source: en.wikipedia.org Pride of America infobox ('Propulsion: Two Rolls-Royce Mermaid pods; Three Rolls-Royce bow thrusters')

zones.what: Three Rolls-Royce bow thrusters are mounted forward and low in the hull, used heavily during the ship's frequent port arrivals/departures on its Hawaii inter-island itinerary.
zones.effect: Deck 4 forward cabins — the lowest and most forward guest deck — are the closest to thruster noise/vibration, which is most noticeable during docking maneuvers rather than constantly at sea.
zones.mattersTo: Guests sensitive to mechanical noise during frequent (near-daily) port maneuvers should note Deck 4 forward is closest to this equipment; it's a non-issue once underway.
zones.source: en.wikipedia.org Pride of America infobox ('Three Rolls-Royce bow thrusters')

zones.what: Multiple cruiser threads describe variable inter-island motion; one reviewer reported the ship 'rocked so hard people were tripping over their own feet' and a port call was cancelled due to swell, while others describe calm summer sailing, and a Tripadvisor forum reply advised sensitive guests to 'book a cabin mid-ship' and stayed on Deck 9.
zones.effect: Motion is inconsistent by season/weather rather than a fixed structural trait, but higher decks and far forward/aft cabins will still amplify whatever motion occurs, same as any ship.
zones.mattersTo: Motion-sensitive guests should favor lower-to-mid decks and midship sections, especially outside the calmer summer season; most cruisers report no issues.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com member review ('rocked so hard people were tripping... canceled a port of call') + tripadvisor.com Honolulu forum thread ('book a cabin mid-ship... stayed on deck nine')

zones.what: Some Deck 7 cabins are interconnecting, and a Cruise Critic top-10-tips reviewer specifically warned that their cabin was 'an inter connecting room, so you hear almost every sound from room 7012.'
zones.effect: Interconnecting cabins carry conversation and TV noise through the connecting door much more than a standard shared wall.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting privacy/quiet should ask specifically whether their cabin has a connecting door, not just what's above/below/beside it; families wanting to book adjoining rooms benefit from the same feature.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com member review ('Pride of America-top 10 tips') citing cabin 7012

leads.claim: Guest reported loud metallic banging noise (like 'hitting a metal garbage can with a baseball bat') coming from below the cabin for the first two nights of the cruise; source of noise (mechanical/crew space) not identified.
leads.source: boards.cruisecritic.com thread '4550 Noisy: What's below deck 4?'

leads.claim: Cabins sit directly above the Deck 6 Mardi Gras Cabaret Lounge & Nightclub; one reviewer of 7526 said they'd 'choose deck 8 or above' on a future cruise to avoid it.
leads.source: boards.cruisecritic.co.uk cabin-location thread + gangwaze.com cabin 9656 review

leads.claim: Interconnecting cabin; neighboring guest reported hearing 'almost every sound' through the connecting door.
leads.source: cruisecritic.com 'Pride of America-top 10 tips' member review

leads.claim: Praised as a 'great position - no noise and close to lifts,' i.e. quiet despite elevator proximity.
Aft-facing family suite on Deck 10, positioned under the Moderno Churrascaria restaurant; reviewer specifically noted 'noise was NOT an issue.'
Balcony cabin directly below the buffet restaurant on Deck 11; reviewer reported audible noise from above in late night and early morning hours.
Deck 9 midship balcony cabin recommended by a forum poster specifically for motion-sensitive travelers; guest 'slept through an apparently rough night.'
This specific cabin has a porthole window instead of the picture window standard to its category.
Wheelchair-accessible oceanview staterooms, larger than standard at 222 sq ft versus 144 sq ft for the category.
leads.source: cruiseline.com Pride of America OA cabin category page

leads.cabins: SQ/SJ category obstructed-view family suites (approx. 4 cabins, deck unconfirmed)
leads.claim: Two-room family suites with no balcony whose window looks directly onto a stowed lifeboat.
leads.source: cruisecritic.com editor cabin review + cruisemapper.com cabin category page

unknowns: No evidence found of a 'hump' (cantilevered overhang past the hull line) on this class; may not be architecturally present, but not confirmed either way.
No evidence found of hull taper affecting top-deck (12/13) balconies' downward view; unconfirmed.
No ship-specific source found describing an I-95-style crew corridor or its guest-deck access points for this vessel.
No ship-specific citation found for anchor-chain noise on forward cabins (a common cruise-ship issue generically, but not documented for Pride of America specifically in this research pass).

Exact fore/aft section of the Mardi Gras Cabaret Lounge & Nightclub footprint on Deck 6 (and therefore the precise cabin range on Deck 7 above it) could not be pinned down beyond the specific cabin numbers found in leads.
Whether lifeboat obstruction is worse on the port or starboard side specifically for Deck 7/8 was suggested by one blog (recommending port-side booking) but not independently corroborated.
